elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly states: “Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience.”

elements.element: Customer may terminate on thirty (30) days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: The added clause permits termination “upon thirty (30) days' prior ... notice.”

elements.element: Customer's termination notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly requires “prior written notice to Licensor.”

elements.element: Vendor must refund prepaid fees upon Customer's termination for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added clause provides that “Licensor shall refund ... any prepaid fees” following the convenience termination.

elements.element: The refund must be calculated pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination.
elements.evidence: The refund applies “pro rata” to prepaid fees “for the period after the effective date of termination.”

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during any committed term.
elements.evidence: The clause states that “Licensor shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Initial Period or any renewal term,” covering each committed term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly grants Licensee a termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice period is between sixty (60) and ninety (90) days.
elements.evidence: The operative notice period is thirty (30) days, which is outside the fallback range of 60–90 days.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee charged for Customer's convenience termination does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed for Licensee's convenience termination; instead, the clause requires a pro-rata refund. The conditional cap is therefore satisfied.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The clause prohibits Licensor from terminating for convenience “during the Initial Period or any renewal term,” which is at least as protective as limiting any such termination to term end.

elements.element: Vendor must provide ninety (90) days' prior notice of a permitted term-end convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No operative language requires Licensor to provide 90 days' notice for a term-end convenience termination or non-renewal.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the preferred position: Licensee receives a 30-day written convenience-termination right and a pro-rata refund, while Licensor is barred from convenience termination during every committed term. It does not independently satisfy the fallback because the Customer notice period is 30 rather than 60–90 days and no 90-day Vendor notice requirement is included. The additions are limited to the requested termination protections and do not disturb termination for cause, insolvency rights, or other unrelated terms.
